subject.title: Add a mitos snapshot-fork sandbox provider + fork-warmed-lease fan-out

question: Should Crabbox accept Mitos as a supported built-in provider, and can its snapshot-fork behavior conform to the existing checkpoint/fork contract without a new core capability?
rationale: The generic fan-out workflow is settled, but permanent provider support and the strength of its isolation and live-state guarantees require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Approve adapter-first support
options.body: Implement Mitos behind existing provider interfaces and add core surface only for a demonstrated provider-neutral contract gap.

options.title: Design live-memory capability first
options.body: Define a distinct provider-neutral capability before integration if memory-state inheritance must be an explicit user guarantee.

options.title: Defer Mitos support
options.body: Retain generic fan-out and wait for stable Mitos APIs plus convincing lifecycle, isolation, and cleanup proof.

recommendation.title: Approve adapter-first support
recommendation.body: Implement Mitos behind existing provider interfaces and add core surface only for a demonstrated provider-neutral contract gap.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current provider-neutral fork fan-out and recommendation surfaces most directly affected by this decision.
